findings.title: Meet fallback crashes when no destination calendar is configured
findings.body: When `evt.location` is Google Meet and `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, destructuring produces no first calendar and this direct `.integration` access throws. The previous optional access handled this case, so booking creation now fails instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credential IDs
findings.body: This conditional writes `credentialId` only for calendar results and sets it to `undefined` for video results, even though video creation results carry the credential ID. The booking reference then cannot identify the video credential; cancellation code that requires a reference credential ID skips deleting the meeting, leaving the external video meeting behind.

findings.title: Lark always creates collective events in the first destination calendar
findings.body: The event manager calls `createEvent` for each destination using that host's credential, but this adapter ignores the credential ID and always selects `destinationCalendar[0]`. For a collective event where the first destination belongs to another host or integration, Lark is sent the wrong calendar ID and the Lark host's event is not created in its intended calendar.

findings.title: Office 365 always creates collective events in the first destination calendar
findings.body: The event manager invokes this service once per destination credential, but this method ignores that credential and always uses the first destination's external ID. When another host's Office 365 account is being used, the ID can refer to a different account's calendar, so creation fails or targets the wrong calendar instead of notifying that host.

findings.title: CalDAV creation filters against the first host's calendar only
findings.body: The event manager invokes calendar creation separately for each destination credential, but this service always filters calendars using the first destination. For a later host's CalDAV account, that calendar will generally not be present in its calendar list, so the filter produces no create requests; the method then still returns success, leaving the host without an event.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference
findings.body: In the recurring cancellation path, each booking can now have multiple calendar references, but this lookup chooses only the first one for every updated booking. The code then attempts deletion through the organizer's credentials rather than the credential for each matching host reference. As a result, recurring collective cancellations leave events on other hosts' calendars, while repeatedly targeting the first reference.

findings.title: Google update and delete no longer fall back to the destination calendar
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is null or undefined, this search compares calendar IDs to that nullish value, so it cannot select a configured destination calendar. Updates are sent with an undefined calendar ID, and the equivalent lookup in `deleteEvent` falls back to `primary`, leaving events on the configured calendar untouched. This breaks rescheduling or cancellation for references without a stored external calendar ID.

findings.title: Organization slug is omitted when team billing is disabled
findings.body: This condition is reversed from the previous behavior: when team billing is disabled it spreads an empty object instead of `{ slug }`, so newly created organizations have no slug. When billing is enabled it sets `slug` directly, whereas the existing flow records it as `requestedSlug`. This breaks the expected organization URL/slug creation behavior.

findings.title: Destinations without a credential ID lose their external calendar ID
findings.body: This branch supports destinations with no `credentialId`, but unlike the branch above it calls `createEvent` without `destination.externalId`. `CalendarManager.createEvent` uses that argument to populate the result's `externalId`, which is then stored as the booking reference's `externalCalendarId`. The resulting reference cannot identify the selected calendar for later updates or deletions.

findings.title: Location updates create calendar references without calendar or credential IDs
findings.body: `updateLocation` now builds references from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but the calendar results returned by `CalendarManager.updateEvent` do not populate either field. Consequently, location changes create calendar references with missing destination and credential identifiers, so later operations cannot reliably target the correct host calendar.

findings.title: Rescheduling a booking with multiple calendars deletes only one old event
findings.body: The reschedule merge path now updates all calendar references, but this lookup still selects only one old calendar reference and deletes only that event. With multiple host calendars, the remaining old events are left behind, producing duplicate or stale events after rescheduling.
